h1: Power hammers and planishing hammers — pneumatic, electric and air forging hammers
intro: Hammers for the metal shaper and the blacksmith. Auto body, hot-rod, motorcycle and aircraft panel builders smooth and shape sheet with a planishing hammer — fast, light blows between an upper die and a crowned lower anvil — and with an electric power hammer that has the force to shape, bead and shrink as well; blacksmiths and forges draw out, upset, punch and forge-weld hot stock under a self-contained air hammer that needs no compressor. NovoTech's value-line hammers are built in China to our specification: PPH pneumatic planishing hammers with 12″ and 24″ throats, the UFP-2 planishing hammer and wheel on one stand, the PH-20D and PH-30D electric power hammers with 20″ and 30″ throats, the PIC50 diamond roller former for embossed panels and the C41 air forging hammers from 35 to 165 lb ram. Parts and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.a: A pneumatic planishing hammer (PPH) runs on shop air and delivers fast, light blows that smooth a panel and take out the marks of earlier shaping — the finishing tool of the auto body and restoration shop. An electric power hammer (PH-20D / PH-30D) has variable speed and more force: it shapes as well as planishes, and with shaping dies it shrinks, stretches and beads. Many shops have both.

faq.q: Which throat depth do I need?
faq.a: The throat is the distance from the dies to the frame — it limits how far into a panel you can reach. A 12″ throat suits brackets, patch panels and motorcycle parts; 20 – 24″ most car panels; the 30″ throat of the PH-30D reaches the middle of hoods, roofs and large aircraft and boat skins.

faq.q: What does a planishing hammer need from the compressor?
faq.a: The PPH500 runs at 50 – 100 psi and the PPH-610 at 90 – 120 psi; the foot pedal or the 3-position air flow valve sets the blow rate. Use clean, dry air — a filter, regulator and lubricator at the hammer keep the valve and the piston working.

faq.q: Does an air forging hammer need shop air?
faq.a: No — the C41 hammers are self-contained: a 2 – 9.4 HP motor drives a compressor cylinder in the hammer itself, and that air drives the ram. They stand on a solid concrete foundation — the larger hammers on a separate anvil block of 441 to 1,874 lb — and forge stock heated in a forge. Choose the ram by the largest stock: the 35 – 55 lb rams for blades, tools and ornamental work up to about 1-1/2″ square, the 88 and 165 lb rams for 2 – 2-1/2″ square bar.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
